description: Fix evidence-backed endpoint underuse across both agent platforms. Keep native command execution and ownership rules intact; make deterministic/indexed Hub calls the normal route when applicable and semantic calls explicitly conditional.

acceptance_criteria: Generated MCP schemas and provider instructions use one active-profile capability/action source and never advertise disabled actions.
High-profile defaults enable intended capabilities; lower profiles omit actions below their minimum tier.
Static and installed skill/prompt surfaces contain no stale fixed action lists that contradict the active schema.
Every enabled public MCP tool/action family has a concrete trigger; active-profile filters suppress unavailable actions.
Semantic review, reasoning, exploration, compression, and delegation are recommended only when the action, backend, permissions, and quality gates pass.
Exact repository search, facts, tests, builds, and deterministic checks retain authoritative Hub/native routes.
Runtime permission, host trust/approval, task scope, and quality checks remain authoritative; Laya cannot grant permissions or execute tools.
A typed host contract records provider/version/surface/session ownership, events, commands, permissions, mode, identity, evidence references, and verification state.
Only Hub-managed sessions with verified identity and permissions qualify for host actions; unknown provider state fails closed.

Laya actively participates in eligible low-risk Hub decisions for every connected provider; valid recommendations affect central routing/context, with deterministic fallback for abstention, failure, invalid scope, or low confidence.
Shadow comparison is optional evaluation, not a blanket prerequisite; raw prompts, transcripts, and source are never stored by default.
Provider observations distinguish proposed, simulated, executed, and verified; permission checks remain unknown unless the host actually verifies them.
Unknown/disconnected provider status is reported uncertain and never represented as a verified handshake.
Codex, Antigravity/Gemini, Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code/Copilot, OpenCode when enabled, and extra configured MCP providers have source-backed surface, install, trust, and verification coverage.
Codex plugins/hooks and all provider-specific packages use currently documented layouts; setup preserves user configuration and never auto-trusts host hooks.
Generated API coverage and agent instructions match actual enabled provider/tool inventory; no provider is described as supported beyond its implemented surface.
Focused checks cover changed decision paths and host adapters; live handshake status is recorded separately for each available provider.
task_endpoint_routing.blocker: No actual provider handshake has been verified in this task. The prior Hub plan explicitly deferred concrete adapters; current user steering overrides that deferral. The local Laya service is available but the runtime status read reports model_resident=false.

clarifications.summary: User directs completion of Codex and all other supported providers (including Antigravity and Claude) and explicitly rejects Laya remaining shadow-only.

task_endpoint_routing.description: User explicitly expanded scope from Codex/Antigravity endpoint routing to full active Laya use and complete integration of every provider enabled/advertised by Local AI Hub. Implement one shared local Laya service, consistent MCP and generated instruction routes, current provider plugin/hook/setup formats, truthful per-provider capability and handshake status. Concrete client adapters are now in scope. Preserve deterministic permissions, host trust/approval, bounded privacy, and fallback contracts.
task_endpoint_routing.next_action: Inventory provider setup/manifests/hooks/skills and all Laya callers; then implement active Laya routing and current provider packaging in independently verifiable units.
